# What /assess measures

<!-- Generated by skills/assess/scripts/gen_catalog.py (`make catalog`); do not edit by hand. -->

This page lists every check `/assess` and `/fleet` run, what each one reads, and how it
feeds the maturity model. It is generated from the check manifest
(`skills/assess/checks/core.toml`), the default maturity model
(`skills/assess/levels/default.toml`) and the signal input classes
(`skills/assess/scripts/lib/level_signals.py`), so it changes only when they do. The same
data for machines is [measures.json](../skills/assess/references/measures.json).

Nothing here is a judgement of a team. A gap is the next thing to try, and a check that
could not be read is shown as not measured with its reason: it earns nothing and costs
nothing.

## How evidence is graded

Each signal has an input class: what its producer read. The class fixes a grade. Conditions graded measured or verified count toward a level; conditions graded config_only or declared are listed, not counted.

| Grade | Input classes | Counts toward a level |
|---|---|---|
| `config_only` | `config_text` | no, listed |
| `declared` | `head_text` | no, listed |
| `measured` | `execution_artifact`, `git_history`, `head_structure` | yes |
| `verified` | `ci_executed`, `platform` | yes |

A scan that feeds no maturity-model criterion is `unclassified` until its evidence is classified (#789 step 6).

## Maturity-model rows

Each row holds conditions in order. A condition holds when all of its criteria hold, and its key is `<row>.<n>:<signal>`.

### Layer 0: agent instructions

Row `layer-0-instructions`, team scope, aggregated by `min`.

| Condition | Criterion | Grade | Counts | Next step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `layer-0-instructions.1` An instruction file is committed | A committed instruction file exists: is true (`layer_grades.instruction_file_present eq true`) | `declared` | no, listed | Commit a CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md that tells an agent how this repository works. |
| `layer-0-instructions.2` An instruction file names a check command | Instruction files name a check command: is above 0 (`agent_environment.check.named_total gt 0`) | `declared` | no, listed | Name the command that checks a change (for example make check) in your instruction file. |
| `layer-0-instructions.2` Every checkable instruction claim holds | Instruction claims that do not hold: is 0 (`instruction_claims.failed eq 0`) | `measured` | yes | Update the instruction lines whose claims no longer match the repository. |
| `layer-0-instructions.2` Always-loaded instructions fit in 200 lines | Always-loaded Claude Code instruction lines: is at most 200 (`nested_instructions.budget.claude_code.lines lte 200`) | `measured` | yes | Move detail that is needed only sometimes into files the instructions point to. |

## Scans

Every scan name `assess_signals.py --scans` accepts, in run order.

### `agent_ops`: Agent-operations guardrails

Committed permission allowlists, hooks, sandbox rules and routine definitions.

- Collector: `core.agent_ops`, reading `repo_root`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; no string field kept.
- Used by: row `layer-8-agent-ops`.
- Evidence: `agent_ops.summary.permissions_encoded` config_text (config_only), `agent_ops.summary.hooks_present` config_text (config_only), `agent_ops.summary.routines_present` config_text (config_only).
- Not measured when: it cannot read its input; the block says why.

### `review_reality`: Review on merged changes

Review and approval shares over the sampled merged changes, read through gh or glab.

- Collector: `core.review_reality`, reading `merged_sample`, `gitlab_note_facts`.
- Network: yes, GitHub or GitLab (with --platform).
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `review_reality.reason` drop.
- Used by: row `layer-7-review`.
- Evidence: `review_reality.reviewed_share` platform (verified), `review_reality.approved_share` platform (verified).
- Not measured when:
  - `network`: A headless run without --platform makes no GitHub or GitLab read. Run fleet or assess_signals.py with --platform, or /assess, with gh or glab signed in.
  - `no_remote`: The repository has no GitHub or GitLab remote, so there are no merged changes to read. Nothing to change if the repository is local only; with a GitHub or GitLab remote, /assess and fleet --platform read its merged changes.

### `coverage_gate`: Coverage gate

Finds coverage thresholds written in CI, task-runner and tool config, each with its file, line and threshold.

- Network: no.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `coverage_gate.gates.form` drop, `coverage_gate.gates.metric` token, `coverage_gate.gates.tool` token, `coverage_gate.gates.unit` token, `coverage_gate.not_detected` drop, `coverage_gate.unmeasured_reason` token.
- Used by: row `layer-6-coverage`.
- Evidence: `coverage_gate.threshold_meets_minimum` config_text (config_only).
- Not measured when:
  - `go_rust_gate_form_not_read`: No coverage gate was found, and the repository holds a go.mod or Cargo.toml: its gate may be a script comparing go tool cover (or a report) to a number, which this scan does not read. Nothing to change if a script gates coverage. To have it measured, set the threshold in go-test-coverage's .testcoverage.yml, cargo tarpaulin --fail-under or cargo llvm-cov --fail-under-lines.

### `ci_checks`: CI runs a test or lint command

Whether a GitHub Actions or GitLab CI line runs a test or lint command, whether one can fail its job on ordinary changes (not masked, not off the ordinary triggers), and whether such a line runs a linter; null when no check is found but a CI file pulls its jobs from elsewhere. Null too when no check is found and a CI system the scan does not parse (Jenkins, CircleCI, Azure Pipelines, Bitbucket Pipelines, Travis CI, Buildkite) is tracked.

- Collector: `core.ci_checks`, reading `repo_root`, `ghsync_root`, `gitlab_merged_ci`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `ci_checks.basis` token, `ci_checks.enforced_basis` token, `ci_checks.includes.id` id, `ci_checks.includes.kind` token, `ci_checks.includes.ref_basis` token, `ci_checks.includes.status` token, `ci_checks.lint_basis` token, `ci_checks.merged_config` token, `ci_checks.merged_config_reason` token, `ci_checks.reason` drop.
- Used by: row `layer-3-linters`, row `layer-5-ci`.
- Evidence: `ci_checks.lint_runs` ci_executed (verified), `ci_checks.enforced_check_runs` ci_executed (verified).
- Not measured when:
  - `included_jobs`: A CI file pulls its jobs from a file this checkout does not hold, so the check may live there. Nothing to change: this reads as not measured until the included file can be read. On GitLab, fleet --platform reads the merged configuration through the CI lint API.
  - `merged_config_partial`: GitLab's merged CI configuration was read and runs no check, but it may lack jobs: an include under rules: or a trigger: child pipeline is not expanded by the lint API. Nothing to change: a check in a conditional include or child pipeline is not read, so this stays not measured rather than reading false.
  - `unknown_trigger`: In enforced_basis: an unmasked check sits in a workflow or job whose triggers this reader cannot settle (no on: key, a rules: if: on a custom variable). Nothing to change if it runs on every change; naming push or pull_request, or a merge request rule, lets the scan read it.
  - `check_target`: In lint_basis: no CI line calls a linter, but one runs a check target or script that may run one inside it (make check, npm test, tox, ./scripts/test.sh, pre-commit run); recipes are not read. Nothing to change if the target lints; calling the linter in its own CI step (ruff check ., make lint) lets the scan read it.
  - `unread_ci_system`: In basis, enforced_basis and lint_basis: no readable GitHub Actions or GitLab CI line settles the signal, and the tree tracks a CI file of a system this scan does not parse (Jenkins, CircleCI, Azure, Bitbucket, Travis CI, Buildkite); unread_ci_files counts them. Nothing to change: the scanner cannot read Jenkins, CircleCI, Azure Pipelines, Bitbucket Pipelines, Travis CI or Buildkite configuration, so their checks read as not measured rather than absent.
